analysis: The PR changes only documentation: CHANGELOG.md (units 15-17, shown as head text with no diff markers) and docs/architecture/scheduling.md (a freshness-stamp bump to 2026-10-11 plus a new paragraph at roughly lines 47-57). The new paragraph says the ordinary catalog picker (Start.pickerSelectionFitsBudget in StartCommand+Picker.swift) checks each model's load estimate separately against the serving set's activation floor and nominal unified cap. It says the picker neither samples live availability nor replaces the configured-reserve, outstanding-load or post-load serviceability gates. Nothing touches authentication, encryption, attestation, billing, App Attest or the coordinator-to-provider boundary, so I found no concrete security regression and no invalidated assumption. The changelog excerpts are existing historical entries and are consistent with the threat model, for example the T-051 profiler references and the cache scope notes for T-041. One coverage limit: the picker source file was not supplied. I cannot confirm that the documented behavior (checking models separately so that models taking turns are allowed) is safe against a provider overcommitting memory. That would be an availability or capacity issue for T-016/T-029-style threats, and it should be checked if the code change ships in a separate PR. I did not verify the CHANGELOG claims against code. The one remaining concern is the cross-file doc-versus-code gap for the picker.
